verses.text: For the chief musician, with flutes. A psalm by David. LORD, listen to my words. Pay attention to what I’m thinking deep down.
Hear me crying out, my King and my God. You’re the one I pray to.
LORD, you’ll hear my voice in the morning. I’ll lay my requests before you first thing and watch for your answer.
You’re a God who takes no pleasure in wrongdoing. Evil can’t make its home with you.
The arrogant can’t stand in your sight. You hate all who do wrong.
You’ll destroy those who tell lies. The LORD detests anyone who’s out for blood or deals in deceit.
But because your faithful love is so great, I’ll come into your house. I’ll bow toward your holy temple in reverence for you.
LORD, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies. Make your way straight in front of me.
There’s nothing trustworthy in what they say. Their hearts are set on destruction. Their throats are open graves, and their tongues are full of flattery.
Hold them guilty, God. Let their own schemes bring them down. Drive them out for all the wrong they’ve done, because they’ve rebelled against you.
Let everyone who takes refuge in you celebrate. Let them always shout for joy, because you defend them. Let those who love your name find joy in you.
You bless the righteous, LORD. You surround them with your favor like a shield.
